// diagnostic

E1308

`run`'s parameter isn't a CLI-derived type

What

`run`'s parameter isn't a CLI-derived type

Why

A typed `fn run(args: T)` entry only works when `T` is a `#CLI`-derived program struct.

Fix

Mark the program struct `#CLI`, or use a direct scalar-parameter `fn run` entry.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1308: tests/ui/result_handler_type_mismatch.stderr.

Error [E1308]: `run`'s parameter isn't a CLI-derived type
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_type_mismatch.jet:1:15
    |
  1 | fn run(value: Int!) {
    |               ^^^^
 Why: a typed `fn run(args: T)` entry only works when `T` is a `#[CLI]`-derived program struct.
 Fix: mark the program struct `#[CLI]` (or `#CLI(Standard)` for the standard pack)
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1308

Error [E0124]: this `if`'s branches produce different types: Int (a whole number) and String (text)
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_type_mismatch.jet:2:15
    |
  2 |     result :: value ? ok -> 1 ! error -> "bad"
    |               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: an `if` used as a value must give the same type on every path (S68)
 Fix: make both branches produce Int (a whole number) (or the same type)
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0124

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_type_mismatch.jet:3:5
    |
  3 |     print(result)
    |     ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116
